about.title: About and limitations
about.purpose: A bilingual, evidence-first assistant for the Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas Rules, 2012. Every answer points to cited rule text with an explicit status.
about.limitsTitle: What is and is not verified

limits.l1: All ingested rule text is currently unverified by a human reviewer, so answers are pointers, not confirmed answers.
limits.l2: No regulatory calculation exists yet: setbacks, FAR/coverage, height, parking and fees are not evaluated.
limits.l3: Only English text is searchable; Hindi questions are matched against English rules.
limits.l4: The amendment to Rule 2(5)(c) is pending verification and its effective date is unknown.
limits.l5: Retrieval is keyword-based and conservative; some valid questions may return no result.
limits.l6: This tool is not an official approval, legal advice or a compliance determination.

setup.step1Body: In backend/.env (or your host's environment) set PII_HASH_SECRET to a long random string and PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the public https address of this server, then restart it.
setup.step2Body: Create a WhatsApp Business app in Meta for Developers. Set WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET, WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID and a WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN of your choice. Register this webhook URL with the same verify token and subscribe to “messages”:
setup.step3Body: Set TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, buy a voice number and point its Voice webhook (HTTP POST) to:
setup.step4Body: On the Status tab run “Check provider connections”. It makes real read-only calls, only for providers you have configured.
setup.step5Body: Send a WhatsApp message and call the number from a phone you control. Confirm the answers cite a rule and page, then send STOP to confirm it goes quiet.
setup.note: Until step 5 has been done with the real providers, treat WhatsApp and phone as untested. A server on your own computer needs a public https tunnel for Meta and Twilio to reach it.

assistant.body: Ask in your own words, in English or Hindi, by typing or speaking, and listen to the answer.
assistant.b: Rule number, page and exact wording as proof
assistant.c: Asks for what is missing instead of guessing

assess.title: Plot Assessment
assess.body: Enter your plot, road and building details and compare them with the limits in the rules.
assess.b: Possible violations with what to change

visual.title: Building Visualization
visual.body: A 3D house generated from your own numbers, on your plot, beside the road.
visual.a: Watch it built from foundation to roof
visual.b: Rotate, zoom, inspect floor by floor
visual.c: Setbacks and dimensions drawn to scale

calc.title: Area Calculator
calc.body: Plot area, floor-area ratio and open-space limits worked out from the rule tables.
calc.a: Area in sq m, sq ft and more
calc.b: Maximum floor area and per-floor area
calc.c: Front and rear open space for your road

s1.title: Ask or enter your plot
s1.body: Type or speak a question, or fill in plot size, road width, building use, height and floors.

s2.title: See your building
s2.body: The workbench draws the plot and builds your house in 3D, with the open spaces from the rules marked on the ground.

s3.title: Check the rules
s3.body: Get a plain-language answer with the rule and page, and a list of what fits, what may not, and what is still missing.

final.title: Ready to plan your building?
final.body: Start with the workbench. It works straight away, and an account lets you keep what you build.
final.p1: Built on the Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas Rules, 2012 (consolidated to March 2025).
final.p2: Every figure points to its rule number and page so you can check it yourself.
final.p3: The rule text is not yet human-verified: results are guidance, never an approval.

ask.title: Ask about the rules
ask.body: Type or speak a question in English or Hindi, for example “What front open space applies on a 9 m road?”. You get a plain-language answer with the rule number and page.
ask.tip: Use the microphone to speak, and the Listen button to hear any answer.

inputs.title: Enter your plot and building
inputs.body: Fill in the project inputs: plot width and length, road width, building use, height, floors and where the building sits on the plot.
inputs.tip: Not sure of a value? Leave it empty. The tool asks for what it needs and never guesses.

visual.title: See it in 3D
visual.body: The workbench builds your house from those numbers. Press Play to watch it go up, drag to rotate, and pick a floor to look inside.
visual.tip: The 3D model is an illustration, not a verified design.

check.title: Check the rules
check.body: Press “Evaluate compliance” to compare your numbers with the setback and floor-area limits, see possible violations, and what to change.
check.tip: Results are guidance. The rule text is not yet human-verified, so the clerk or authority decides.

capabilities.title: What NirmaanSetu can do for you
capabilities.body: I explain the Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas Rules in plain words, check your plot against them, and show your house in 3D. Ask me anything about the rules or about how to use the app.
capabilities.s1: Ask a rule question in English or Hindi and I answer with the rule number and page.
capabilities.s2: Enter your plot and building details in the Workbench to see your house in 3D and a compliance check.
capabilities.s3: Use the Calculator for permissible floor area and open spaces.
capabilities.s4: Create a free account to save projects and come back to them.

start.title: How to get started
start.body: The quickest way is the Workbench: type your plot size, then ask a question.
start.s2: Enter plot width and length, road width and building height (or press Example).
start.s3: Ask a question, for example “What front open space applies?”.
start.s4: Press Evaluate compliance to compare your numbers with the rule text.

workbench.title: Using the 3D Workbench
workbench.body: The Workbench builds your house from the numbers you enter, so every change updates the model.
workbench.s1: Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan; use the Front, Rear, Left, Right and Top buttons for fixed views.
workbench.s2: Press Play to watch the house being built from the foundation upwards; Replay and Reset restart it.
workbench.s3: Pick a floor to cut the building open and see an illustrative room layout.
workbench.s4: Switch to Site plan or Floor plan for 2D drawings with measurements.

assessment.title: Checking your plot against the rules
assessment.body: Evaluate compliance compares your front and rear gaps and floor area with limits taken from the rule tables. It never gives a pass mark: it shows possible violations, what is missing and what is not checked.
assessment.s1: Fill in plot, road and building details.
assessment.s3: Read each item: possible violation, within limit, needs input or not evaluated.

calculator.title: Calculator
calculator.body: The Calculator gives the permissible floor area, front and rear open space and the depth left for building, plus a plain plot-area calculator.
calculator.s1: Enter plot width and length (or area) and the road width.
calculator.s3: Each number shows the rule it came from.

account.title: Account and saving projects
account.body: You can ask questions, use the Workbench and the Calculator without an account. An account lets you save projects and assessments.
account.s1: Choose Create account and enter your name, e-mail and a password of at least 8 characters with a letter and a number.
account.s2: Forgot your password? Use “Forgot password?” on the sign-in page to get a reset link by e-mail.
account.s3: Sign out any time from the menu with your name.

voice.title: Voice: speaking and listening
voice.body: Press the microphone to ask by voice, and “Listen” under any answer to hear it read aloud, in English or Hindi.
voice.s1: Allow the microphone when the browser asks. Chrome and Edge work best.
voice.s2: Use Pause, Resume and Stop while an answer is read.
voice.s3: Hindi read-aloud needs a Hindi voice installed on your device.

language.title: Hindi and English
language.body: The whole app works in Hindi and English. Switch with EN / हिं at the top, or just type or speak your question in Hindi.
language.s1: Questions in Devanagari are answered in Hindi.
language.s2: Rule text is quoted exactly as it appears in the official document, which is in English.
language.s3: Your language choice is remembered in this browser.

rulebook.title: Rulebook and sources
rulebook.body: Every answer is based on the Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas Rules, 2012 (consolidated to 6 March 2025). You can search the rules and see the source pages.
rulebook.s1: Open Rulebook & sources to search by rule number or words.
rulebook.s2: Each answer shows the rule number and page; tap it to read the exact text.
rulebook.s3: A reported 2026 amendment is listed but not applied, because its official text is not available.

limits.title: How far to trust an answer
limits.body: NirmaanSetu is a guide, not an approval. The rule text has not been checked by a human reviewer yet, so figures should be confirmed on the official page, and the permission authority decides.
limits.s1: You always see the rule number and page behind an answer.
limits.s2: When the rules do not answer a question, I say so instead of guessing.
limits.s3: A 3D model is an illustration of your numbers, not a verified design.

greeting.title: Hello! I'm your NirmaanSetu assistant
greeting.body: I explain the Madhya Pradesh building rules in simple words and help you plan your plot. Tell me about your plot, or ask a question like the ones below.

thanks.title: You're welcome
thanks.body: Happy to help. If you have another question about your plot or the building rules, just ask.

journey.title: Building a home from scratch: where to start
journey.body: Here is a simple path with this app. It is guidance to help you plan, not an approval: your local permission office decides.
journey.s1: Enter your plot width, depth and the width of the road in front of it (left panel), or just describe the plot in the question box.
journey.s2: Press Evaluate Compliance to see the open-space and floor-area limits that apply to your plot, each with its rule number and page.
journey.s3: Add the house you have in mind (height, floors, footprint) to see it on your plot in 3D and what to change.
journey.s4: Ask me about any rule in English or Hindi, for example open space, floor area or fees.
journey.s5: Print the report and take it to your local permission office. They tell you the documents needed and give the approval.

vguide.script: Welcome to NirmaanSetu. On the left, enter your plot size, road width and building details. You can also type or speak a question in the box at the top, in English or Hindi. The middle shows your plot and house in three dimensions. On the right, press Check my plot to see which rules apply, with the rule number and page as proof. This is guidance only. The clerk decides.
